identity.title: Rash, fever, arthralgia after new drug (AIN triad)

technique.how: Ask about every drug started in the preceding days to weeks (β-lactams and other antibiotics, PPIs, NSAIDs, sulfonamides, allopurinol, checkpoint inhibitors), the timing of AKI relative to the start, and accompanying fever, maculopapular rash, arthralgia or flank pain; examine the skin. Ask specifically about PPIs, whose AIN is typically silent.
technique.prerequisites: Complete medication reconciliation with start dates.

interpretation.positive_finding: New drug exposure with fever, rash or arthralgia and otherwise unexplained AKI supports drug-induced AIN, but each feature is present in only a minority of biopsy-proven cases (arthralgia 45%, fever 30%, rash 21%). Sterile pyuria/WBC casts add support.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of the triad is the norm — most biopsy-proven AIN, especially PPI-induced, lacks these features. Do not exclude AIN on their absence.
interpretation.pitfalls: Features overlap with sepsis, drug fever and vasculitis; eosinophiluria and gallium scanning have limited diagnostic utility (PMID 20517290, Abstract). Only kidney biopsy is definitive.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive → stop the suspect drug now, urinalysis for WBC casts, nephrology re: biopsy/steroids; negative → still review the drug list in unexplained AKI.

estimates.target_condition: Biopsy-proven acute interstitial nephritis (92% drug-related) — fever at presentation; sensitivity only, no non-AIN comparison group
estimates.population: 60 adults with AIN identified among 2,598 native renal biopsies over 12 years at one Irish centre; 58% needed acute RRT
estimates.reference_standard: Native kidney biopsy showing interstitial inflammatory infiltrate
estimates.quote: The presenting symptoms included oliguria (51%), arthralgia (45%), fever (30%), rash (21%) and loin pain (21%).

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use absent rash/fever/arthralgia to exclude AIN in AKI on a new drug.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Rash with mucosal involvement, facial edema or systemic features (DRESS/SJS) plus AKI → stop the drug urgently and seek specialist input.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: History items; no reliability data found.

extraction_notes: Anchor PMID 20517290 confirmed (Perazella & Markowitz 2010 narrative review); its abstract contains no triad frequency, so the widely cited 'classic triad in ~10%' is (unverified recall) and not entered. Primary series located: Clarkson 2004 (PMID 15340098; abstract gives individual feature frequencies among biopsy-proven AIN, entered as three sensitivity-only estimates — no specificity because no non-AIN comparison group, so no LR can be computed) and Muriithi 2014 (PMID 24927897; abstract: drugs 70% of AIN, PPI patients 'less symptomatic', no feature percentages). No diagnostic-accuracy study with a control group was found ('biopsy-proven acute interstitial nephritis clinical features case series'; 'Clarkson acute interstitial nephritis clinical features corticosteroid'; 'Muriithi acute interstitial nephritis 1993-2011'). The composite triad itself is not quantified; only its components. Status partially_quantified.
